changelog: Insert a narrow, surface-form rule after C2 to forbid cuts that split a main verb from its essential complement (addresses the primary finding about predicate–argument separation).
findings: The prompt underrates cuts that separate a predicate (main verb) from its essential complements/arguments, so it allows splits that leave an earlier stretch whose truth or reference depends on a following object, clausal complement, or prepositional complement.

The prompt fails to recognise post‑nominal modifiers and complements (relative clauses, 'from/in which' PPs, appositives, titles) as part of the noun they complete, permitting cuts before them that break noun identity or scope.

edits.was: - At each cut, judge whether translating the left and right pieces independently
edits.now: - Do not cut immediately after a main verb when the next token begins its essent

diagnosis.why: The new surface rule forbidding cuts immediately after main verbs made the model avoid splitting verb+complement sequences, which improved cohesion for longer/complex spans (bins >7) but displaced cuts into adjacent very short pieces and enumerations, worsening many ≤5-token cases; net effect is near-zero but slightly negative.
diagnosis.lesson: A verb–complement prohibition helps longer/more complex pieces but harms very short pieces (≤5 tokens); a later revision should avoid applying it indiscriminately across small latency bins.
